name: Mother Shucker
looks: Midge emerger: dark slim body, round thorax, white wing nub and a trailing shuck.
fix: Mother Shucker: a grey or tan foam strip tied along the shank and extending about one hook length past the bend as the shuck; a short grizzly hackle splayed FLAT (parachute/hackle-stacker style) with white post material folded over it; straight dry-fly hook. The current image has an upright swept-back grizzly collar and a black blade-like body.

name: Frenchie
looks: Slim pheasant-tail body with a bright pink bead and a hot orange collar.
fix: Frenchie on a jig hook: reddish-brown PHEASANT-TAIL fibre abdomen with a copper wire rib, a coq de León tail (speckled rooster fibres), a pink ice-dub hot-spot collar behind a slotted tungsten bead (bronze/gold). The current image has a grey-taupe fur body, which is wrong.

name: Black Beauty
looks: Slim black body, silver rib, black bead and a small round thorax.
fix: Black Beauty (Pat Dorsey): slim black thread body with about seven open turns of fine COPPER wire, a small black dubbed head, NO bead, on a curved hook (TMC 2487 style). The current image uses silver wire and reads as a Zebra Midge.

name: Sow bug
looks: Flat, wide and oval with ribbed segments like an armadillo.
fix: Sow bug: a LOW, FLAT, OVAL body seen side-on, grey dubbing under a flat shell back, wire rib, short picked-out legs, on a straight or only slightly curved hook. The current image is tall, humped and curved like a scud.

name: Zonker
recipe: Rabbit-strip wing • flashy body • stripped hackle
looks: Slim silver body topped with a long rabbit-strip wing that trails far past the hook.
fix: Zonker: silver Mylar tubing body with slightly frayed rear end; the white rabbit strip is tied in at the head AND tied down at the rear of the body with visible thread wraps, then flows back as the tail; a soft white or grizzly hackle collar behind the head. The current image's strip is only tied at the head and has no collar.
